summary:
No decision was reached. 20 open questions, 23 open blockers, 3 people took an explicit position on an option.

## The main point

The meeting walked through the architecture of clinical intelligence, member orchestration, and related platforms, and Ratnakar wanted the group to resolve a business-ownership question at the end. Two issues remained unresolved: who should own enterprise-wide orchestration (a single constituent or a consortium), and whether to build clinical journeys internally, use AI such as ChatGPT Health, partner with a vendor, or acquire a company. Catherine said the company is not moving fast enough and proposed a smaller follow-up session to define capabilities and accountable leaders; Ratnakar said the group should map stakeholders and assess what is ready, but did not confirm Catherine's proposed date. Mark asked what the initiative is specifically solving for, echoing Catherine's point that no actual member interventions were specified, and that question was not answered. Mark put the opportunity at "$700 million, over a billion dollars."

## Presented, no challenge recorded

- Monique explained that clinical intelligence is a single enterprise-shared capability that turns clinical, claims, and social data into context, signals, and predictions.
- Venkat explained that the data foundation centralizes administrative data (claims, eligibility, provider, grievances) and that clinical data enters through HealthOS, including EMRs and ADT/discharge records.
- Saurabh presented that effective member engagement journeys require clinical knowledge and that the journey-building platform is low-code/no-code, enabling fast time to market.
- Vikram presented that standardizing how models are built, consumed, and deployed would enable advanced architectures such as transformers.

## Open questions

- Ratnakar asked how member orchestration, Health OS, TMB, TextQL, and clinical intelligence fit together and what each is for relative to member journeys and clinical outcomes.
- Ratnakar and Catherine asked who will be the single accountable business leader for clinical intelligence and member orchestration, or whether a consortium governs it.
- Catherine asked what the actual member interventions are — when, how, and on what topic the company engages a member.
- Kristy asked which redundant member outreach capabilities get shut off as part of consolidating the platform.
- Ratnakar asked why separate analytics tools are needed, and how to determine which model actually drives the right outcome.

## Where people stand

- Ratnakar: wants to move forward with the Caroline Data Foundation; proposes using AI to rapidly generate clinical journeys as a faster alternative to a vendor; conditionally supports acquiring a company if a great one is found; wants a small group to debate single-constituent versus consortium ownership.
- Catherine: supports the Caroline Data Foundation as "a great foundation to be building"; is worried about speed; raised the possibility of an external partner but said "I don't actually have a dog in that fight"; wants clarity on what is being solved and who is accountable before next steps.
- Mark: expressed "full commitment" to the platform work; wants a follow-up meeting soon and "not another Friday night"; asked what the initiative is specifically solving for.
- Kristy: wants to map what outreach is happening today before taking next steps; wants APIs or shared visibility so teams can see who is engaging a member and avoid simultaneous contact.
- Saurabh: wants clinicians to shape the journeys being built; said "let's not give that up" regarding direct clinical and consumer relationship.
- Stephen: proposed parsing capabilities into smaller areas so single accountable owners can be assigned; said "open to whatever path we take, obviously."
- Ashok: supports a platform-centric approach; said a vendor could accelerate delivery as long as member data is protected within the company's ecosystem.
- Monique: said "I'm bullish, certainly, on our ability to mature that" regarding behavioral science for member engagement.
- Vikram said "Why solve a problem already solved?"
- No explicit position recorded from Edwige.

## What is blocking progress

- The group has no shared answer to what specific member interventions the platform will orchestrate, which Catherine said must be defined before next steps (raised by Catherine).
- No single accountable business owner or governance model for enterprise-wide orchestration has been identified (raised by Ratnakar and Stephen).
- A unique person ID across entities must be enabled in Caroline before cross-entity member orchestration can work (raised by Ashok).
- No method exists yet to determine which of the many existing models actually drives the right outcome (raised by Ratnakar).
- Multiple teams are reaching the same members simultaneously with no shared visibility, and the connected data dots are "not clean" (raised by Kristy and Ratnakar).

## Next steps

- Mark committed: "You've got my full commitment to backless work."
- Ratnakar will outline the tech constituent on his side.
- Ratnakar will outline who all the constituents are.
- Ratnakar will outline how the company will outreach to members and outline the clinical journeys, and will share this with tech-side stakeholders and business-side stakeholders.

## Awaiting a reply
